# cHardwareGP8 (hw_type 4) test-CPU traces by the C++ reference
# (cbuild/work/avida -a, analyze LOAD_SEQUENCE... + TRACE trace_out/ 0
# <update> <random>), one BATCH per reference run:
# BATCH <config dir under tests/fixtures> <fixed|random inputs> <update>
# INST <name>  (the instruction set, INSTSET diff:hw_type=4)
# SEQ <sequence> <fnv1a64 of the trace> <trace length in bytes>
# One world RNG and one test CPU carry over from genome to genome within a
# batch, as in cAnalyze::CommandTrace; each fixture batch keeps the first
# sequences of its run (at most 5; a prefix keeps the RNG sequence).
# Random batches hold nop-A..nop-H plus up to 54 other instructions of the library,
# 100-instruction genomes drawn uniformly; every reference run of a random
# batch traced 40 genomes and all 40 Rust traces matched. Left out everywhere:
# die (the reference segfaults in a test CPU). Left out in configs without
# forage targets (exp_env/abs1, abs2av, gene_env/mut1, div2, thr, misc1):
# set-forage-target, set-ft-once, set-rand-ft-once (folding a target with
# no resource targets divides by zero and dereferences an empty set's
# begin() in C++; Err in Rust). The last batches are hand-written genomes
# (self-replicators over set-memory / h-copy / divide-memory, repro,
# threads, I/O, movement) in each config, and in exp_env/ft1 genomes that
# put INT_MIN into the forage-target, look-direction and rotate registers
# (the reference binary folds abs(INT_MIN) as 2^31).
BATCH exp_env/abs1 fixed -1
INST nop-A
INST nop-B
INST nop-C
INST nop-D
INST nop-E
INST nop-F
INST nop-G
INST nop-H
INST swap
INST one
INST sg-rotate-r
INST look-around-ex
INST get-forage-target
INST mult
INST nand
INST if-less
INST rotate-x
INST mov-head
INST wait-cond-equ
INST inc
INST rotate-away-org-id
INST if-gtr-0
INST look-again-ex
INST rand
INST yield

INST wait-cond-less
INST h-copy

INST dec
INST search-seq-d
